{{Short description|Mathemical concept}}
In [[hyperbolic geometry]], the '''Meyerhoff manifold''' is the [[arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifold]] obtained by <math>(5,1)</math> [[Dehn surgery|surgery]] on the [[Figure-eight knot (mathematics)|figure-8]] [[knot complement]].  It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Meyerhoff|first=Robert|year=1987}} as a possible candidate for the hyperbolic 3-manifold of smallest volume, but the [[Weeks manifold]] turned out to have  slightly smaller volume. It has  the second smallest volume 
:<math>V_m = 12\cdot(283)^{3/2}\zeta_k(2)(2\pi)^{-6} = 0.981368\dots</math>
of orientable arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifolds, where <math>\zeta_k</math> is the [[Dedekind zeta function|zeta function]] of the quartic field of discriminant <math>-283</math>. Alternatively,

: <math>V_m = \Im(\rm{Li}_2(\theta)+\ln|\theta|\ln(1-\theta)) = 0.981368\dots</math>

where <math>\rm{Li}_n</math> is the [[polylogarithm]] and <math>|x|</math> is the [[absolute value]] of the complex root <math>\theta</math> (with positive imaginary part) of the [[quartic function|quartic]] <math>\theta^4+\theta-1=0</math>.

{{harvs|txt|last=Chinburg|first=Ted|year=1987}} showed that this manifold is [[Arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifold|arithmetic]].
